linearRegression.explanation: Fits an ordinary least-squares linear model (response = intercept + sum of coefficient x predictor) to 1 to 8 numeric predictors with R's stats::lm, then reopens the saved model in a fresh R process and checks every coefficient, prediction and residual against an independent calculation. It publishes coefficients.csv, training.csv, heldout.csv (when held-out rows are given) and regression-summary.json. Choose it for calibration curves or simple explanatory fits whose error limits you can state in advance.
pitfalls: There must be more training rows than coefficients, and the predictors must not be (nearly) linearly dependent; otherwise RANK_DEFICIENT_DATA or ILL_CONDITIONED_DATA.
Only additive numeric terms: no categorical variables, interactions, polynomials or custom formulas.
No confidence intervals, hypothesis tests or causal claims; held-out errors describe only the rows you supplied.
A correct fit that misses a declared requirement fails with FIT_REQUIREMENT_NOT_MET and is not passed to later workflow steps.

examples.purpose: Known intercept10 and slope2 with independently orthogonal finite residuals and held-out observations.
Change the known slope to3 while retaining the same training/held-out error budget.

fields.explanation: Fit an explicit small numeric additive least-squares model, reopen it natively, and decide whether finite fit/prediction requirements are met. No causal or future-generalisation claim.

/properties/version.explanation: Format identifier of this Schemaxis document; it must be "schemaxis.r/1". It is not the R release.

/properties/operation.explanation: linearRegression fits numeric additive ordinary least squares and publishes independently checked coefficients and predictions.

/properties/predictors.explanation: The 1 to 8 explanatory variables, in the order their values appear in every training and held-out row. Each gets one coefficient in the fitted model.

/properties/predictors/items.explanation: One predictor: a lowercase name and a unit label. Its position in the list is the column position of its values in each row.

/properties/predictors/items/properties/.explanation: Distinct lowercase predictor/response identifier; intercept is reserved. Native formulas use fixed x1…xN/y symbols, so this label never becomes executable R syntax.
Plain unit label, such as V or degC, retained for scientific interpretation. No conversion, dimensional-consistency proof or physical calibration is performed.

/properties/response.explanation: Observed dependent numeric quantity with a distinct lowercase name and plain unit label. It is the final cell of every training/held-out row.

/properties/response/properties/name.explanation: Distinct lowercase predictor/response identifier; intercept is reserved. Native formulas use fixed x1…xN/y symbols, so this label never becomes executable R syntax.

/properties/response/properties/unit.explanation: Plain unit label, such as V or degC, retained for scientific interpretation. No conversion, dimensional-consistency proof or physical calibration is performed.

/properties/training.explanation: The 4 to 512 observations used to fit the model; each row lists the predictor values in declared order and then the observed response. The rows must contain more observations than coefficients and enough independent variation in the predictors; a numerical conditioning limit (1e6 after scaling) rejects nearly dependent predictors.
pitfalls: Repeating the same predictor values or using predictors that are multiples of each other cannot be fixed by adding more rows; change the design.

/properties/training/items.explanation: One finite observed row: predictor values in descriptor order, followed by the response value. Width must equal predictor count plus one.

/properties/training/items/items.explanation: Finite numeric cell within ±1e9, in the corresponding authored predictor or response units. No missing values or strings.

/properties/heldout.explanation: Optional one to 512 separate observed rows in the same predictor/response order. These finite rows assess declared prediction errors, not future generalisation; no automatic split.

/properties/heldout/items.explanation: One finite observed row: predictor values in descriptor order, followed by the response value. Width must equal predictor count plus one.

/properties/heldout/items/items.explanation: Finite numeric cell within ±1e9, in the corresponding authored predictor or response units. No missing values or strings.

/properties/intercept.explanation: Include a constant coefficient, default true. Disable only when a zero response at zero predictors is a justified model constraint; training rows must exceed coefficient count.

/properties/requirements.explanation: Optional one to 32 named finite fit requirements. Native computation verification comes first; unmet requirements block success and downstream reuse.

/properties/requirements/items.explanation: One named finite requirement; choose an aggregate error maximum or a signed prediction bound at one declared sample.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/0.explanation: Aggregate RMSE or maximum absolute error over the selected scope, with a nonnegative inclusive maximum in response units.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/0/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters, used in the explained acceptance report.
Choose training or heldout. Held-out requirements require separately authored held-out observed rows; scopes are never silently substituted.

rmse: root-mean-square residual over all rows in scope. maxAbsoluteError: the largest absolute residual (observed minus predicted) in scope. Both are in response units and need only a nonnegative maximum.
Largest acceptable error, 0 to 1e18, in response units; equality passes. The reported margin is maximum minus the measured error, so a negative margin means the requirement is unmet.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/1.explanation: Signed native prediction at a required zero-based sample index, with inclusive minimum, maximum or both in response units.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/1/p.explanation: Unique lowercase requirement identifier, up to 64 characters, used in the explained acceptance report.
Choose training or heldout. Held-out requirements require separately authored held-out observed rows; scopes are never silently substituted.
prediction: bound the model's predicted response for one row of the chosen scope, selected by sampleIndex, rather than an aggregate error.
Zero-based index in the selected declared scope for prediction bounds. It must be present and within the selected row list.
Inclusive lower prediction bound in response units. Signed margin is actual prediction minus minimum; a negative margin is unmet.
Inclusive upper bound on the predicted response at the selected row, in response units; it may be negative. The margin is maximum minus prediction. Give minimum as well to require a range.

/properties/requirements/items/oneOf/1/a.explanation: Lower-bound form: minimum is given, so the prediction must be at least that value; maximum may also be given.
Upper-bound form: maximum is given, so the prediction must not exceed that value; minimum may also be given.
